<description>
This replaces the FreeBSD cross-compilation job with a native build and test job inside a FreeBSD VM. NetBSD and OpenBSD retain their existing cross-compilation jobs.

We currently cross-compile BSD binaries without testing them in this repository. Running tests before merge should help catch platform-specific regressions that would otherwise first appear in nightly builds. This starts with FreeBSD because it has been the most reliable BSD platform in the nightly jobs.

As we don't have native FreeBSD runners, the job uses [vmactions/freebsd-vm](https://github.com/vmactions/freebsd-vm), which is also used by the nightly builds. It reuses the existing CI scripts, depends build, and cache actions where possible.

The VM image is cached after its `prepare` step installs dependencies. The job also restores and saves the usual build caches. Initial testing on free GitHub Actions runners took approximately 60 minutes without caches and 20–30 minutes with caches populated. Performance on Warp runners remains untested.

The VM uses the runner's available CPU count and 75% of its RAM, leaving the remaining memory for the host and VM overhead. There is some overhead after testing while `rsync` copies cache directories back out of the VM.

The patchset also suppresses `lsof` warnings on FreeBSD that would otherwise interfere with functional tests.

Two functional tests are currently excluded:

- `feature_reindex_init` failed during testing.
- `p2p_private_broadcast_retry_v1` took an unusually long time.

Both warrant further investigation.

The job requires enabling one additional action:

```text
vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1
```
</description>

[2026-11-17] rc:4597374839 inline on .github/workflows/ci.yml by willcl-ark (member):
I think sticking with UFS is the better choice here, would you agree?

This means BSD_RELEASE just stays as `15.1`; would you like a code comment next to it?
[2026-11-17] rc:4597589088 inline on .github/workflows/ci.yml by hebasto (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
[quoted text omitted]

If we are going to add a single new job, I’d prefer that it increase our test coverage. A job using 15.1-zfs would be the only one that covers code paths where the `HAVE_POSIX_FALLOCATE` macro is undefined. Of course, this means that the `feature_reindex_init.py` functional test would have to be temporarily disabled until https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/33128 is fixed.
[2026-11-17] rc:4597934163 inline on .github/workflows/ci.yml by fanquake (member):
[quoted text omitted]

Why is increasing test coverage here, dependant on filesystem? We are increasing test coverage in any case?
[2026-11-17] rc:4598201579 inline on .github/workflows/ci.yml by hebasto (member):
[quoted text omitted]

`posix_fallocate()` is [disabled](https://github.com/freebsd/freebsd-src/commit/96ed2690dfb300033e48384704da6ec45737abee) for ZFS on FreeBSD, so this job exercises a code path that none of the other CI jobs currently tests: https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/e211dd0186e9646167d063a16f0da88e5f72e05f/src/util/fs_helpers.cpp#L229-L241
[2026-11-17] rc:4598225249 inline on .github/workflows/ci.yml by fanquake (member):
Sure, but this is also increasing test coverage, by just running any FreeBSD tests.
[2026-11-17] rc:4598240266 inline on .github/workflows/ci.yml by hebasto (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
I mean additional coverage.
[2026-11-17] c:6945393241 comment by hebasto (member) (edited 2026-11-17):
Apparently, `rsync` is very flaky.

That was one of the reasons I dropped Ccache caching from the [nightly builds](https://github.com/hebasto/bitcoin-core-nightly/blob/main/.github/workflows/freebsd.yml).
